html:
A famine in northern Vietnam from late 1944 through 1945 that killed somewhere between 400,000 and 2 million people. Vietnam's own figure is 2 million.

Vietnam was then part of French Indochina, still run by French officials loyal to Vichy France but occupied by Japan. Both took rice by force for their armies and for export, and farmers were made to grow jute and other war crops instead of food. Allied bombing cut the railway and shipping that once brought rice from the south. Bad weather wrecked the harvest in the north.

People starved in the villages of the Red River delta and on the streets of Hanoi. In March 1945 Japan threw out the French administration, but did nothing to stop the dying.

The Viet Minh led raids on granaries and handed out rice, which won it huge support. When Japan surrendered in August, it took power in the August Revolution, and Hồ Chí Minh spoke of the famine in his declaration of independence. The same war brought the Bengal famine to British India.
sum: A famine in northern Vietnam from late 1944 through 1945 that killed somewhere between 400,000 and 2 million people. Vietnam's own figure is 2 million.
